title: Verifiable rewards as fine-tuning: supervised start, then executor rewards only
follows: R1.39 (FAIL: reward-only training from scratch stays at the cue floor)
question: If a model first learns from labels for one third of the steps and then only from the executor's right/wrong signal on its own sampled answers, does it execute programs better out of distribution than the same model trained with labels for all steps?

predictions.PASS: the reward phase (no labels) lifts OOD execution by >= 3 points over labels for all 15,000 steps, without losing more than 2 points in distribution
predictions.RL2: the same for the Transformer (PARTIAL alternative)
predictions.RL4: reported: confident errors OOD rise at most 1.5x (R1.39 showed REINFORCE from scratch destroys calibration)
predictions.fairness: the -rl models see labels for 5,000 steps only; their baselines see labels for all 15,000. The reward uses the label only as an executor's check would (right/wrong of the sampled answer)
predictions.prior: RL from verifiable rewards works as fine-tuning in large models; whether it adds OOD generalisation at this scale is open, and a FAIL is informative

prior_art: REINFORCE (Williams 1992), RL from verifiable rewards as fine-tuning (DeepSeek-R1 2501.12948, Tulu 3 RLVR 2411.15124), R1.39
not_claimed: Verifiable-reward fine-tuning is prior art; the question is only whether it earns a place in Rouge's training recipe at this scale.
